company.name: Pixelhive Studio
company.summary: You run an 18-person creative and digital marketing agency in Berlin. Your team includes designers, copywriters, social media managers, account managers, and one developer. You sell ongoing social campaigns, ad creative, and monthly reporting to clients, with many revision rounds along the way.
offerings: Social media campaign planning and execution
Copywriting for social, ads, and landing pages
Monthly performance reports and client dashboards
Landing page and campaign microsite updates
company.customers: Small and mid-sized consumer brands, local Berlin businesses, ecommerce shops, and startups that need regular marketing execution.

roles.title: Graphic Designer

Export final files in required formats

repetitive_tasks: Review campaign concepts before client delivery
Give feedback on design and copy pairings
Set visual direction for new client pitches

roles.title: Motion Designer

roles.title: Copywriter
repetitive_tasks: Draft social captions and ad headlines

Check copy against brand tone guides

repetitive_tasks: Coordinate post approvals with account managers

strategy.executive_summary: Pixelhive Studio is an 18-person Berlin agency with five designers, three copy and content people, four social media managers, four account managers, one developer, and one operations manager. Most of your current work runs through Meta Business Suite, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, Google Ads, GA4, Looker Studio, Google Workspace, and Slack, with little automation between them. The best near-term gains are in comment and DM triage, client approval chasing, first-draft copy, monthly report data pulls, and ad resize prep. Start with low-effort agents that keep a human in the loop for public replies, client emails, and final numbers.

maturity.label: Early stage
maturity.note: You have the tools in place but the work is still manual. No agents are running, data lives in separate platforms and sheets, and team time is spent on repetition rather than strategy.

opportunities.title: Comments and DMs answered in minutes
opportunities.description: An agent watches comments and direct messages across client accounts, drafts replies from approved FAQs, and flags sensitive or buying-intent threads to the right person. It logs repeated questions so your team can update the FAQ bank.
before: Open Meta Business Suite, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and TikTok one by one.
Copy common answers from a notes doc.
Log repeated questions in a sheet.
after: Agent checks all connected accounts every 15 minutes.
Agent drafts replies for common questions.
Agent flags sensitive threads in Slack with context.
Human: approves or edits drafts and sends replies.
Agent updates the repeated-question log.

opportunities.title: Client approvals chased automatically
opportunities.description: An agent reads client email and Slack threads, pulls out feedback and approvals, and keeps a shared approval tracker current. It sends polite reminders when a client is holding up a deadline.
before: Account manager searches email and Slack for feedback.
Checks which items are still waiting.
Writes reminder emails one by one.
after: Agent reads client email and Slack threads.
Agent extracts feedback, approvals, and open questions.
Agent updates the approval tracker.
Agent drafts reminder emails for late items.
Human: reviews the tracker and sends reminders.

opportunities.title: First drafts for captions and ad variants
opportunities.description: An agent turns a short brief and brand tone guide into first drafts for social captions, headlines, and A/B variants. It marks claims or phrases that need human checking before client delivery.
before: Read the client brief and old posts.
Check every line against the tone guide.
after: Human: writes a 5-line brief.
Agent drafts captions, headlines, and 5 to 10 variants.
Agent checks drafts against the tone guide and flags claims.
Human: edits the best options.
Agent saves approved copy to the client folder.

opportunities.title: Monthly report data pull and first notes
opportunities.description: An agent pulls numbers from each platform and GA4 into a reporting sheet, then writes plain-language notes about what changed. Your team checks the numbers and edits the story before it goes to the client.
before: Log into Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, and GA4.
Build slides or a Looker Studio page.
after: Agent pulls numbers from connected platforms and GA4.
Agent fills the reporting sheet and Looker Studio data source.
Agent drafts plain-language notes on changes.
Human: checks numbers and edits notes.
Agent builds the client-ready report draft.

opportunities.title: Ad resize prep and export names
opportunities.description: An agent reads campaign specs and prepares the resize list, file names, and export checklist for each platform. It reduces the manual admin around exports and gives designers a clean queue.
before: Write a resize list by hand.
Rename files to match naming rules.
after: Agent reads campaign specs and builds the size list.
Agent renames source files and sets export names.
Agent creates the export checklist.
Human: reviews the list and exports final files.
Agent files exports into the right client folders.

opportunities.title: Weekly call recaps and action items
opportunities.description: An agent turns recorded weekly status calls into a short recap with owners and due dates. It posts the recap in the client Slack channel or drafts the follow-up email for the account manager.
before: Write a recap email after the call.
Add action items to the tracker.
after: Agent records and transcribes the call with permission.
Agent writes a short recap with owners and dates.
Agent adds action items to the tracker.
Human: checks names, dates, and tone.
Agent sends the recap or saves it as an email draft.

opportunities.title: Invoice reminders and subscription renewals
opportunities.description: An agent watches invoice due dates and software renewal dates in your finance sheet and inbox. It drafts reminder emails and flags subscriptions that are close to renewal.
before: Check the invoice sheet each week.
Compare due dates to payments received.
after: Agent checks invoice due dates and payment status.
Agent drafts reminder emails for late invoices.
Agent flags upcoming software renewals.
Human: reviews and sends reminders.
Agent updates the finance log.

opportunities.title: Landing page checks before launch
opportunities.description: An agent runs a launch checklist on campaign pages, checking forms, tracking pixels, mobile layout, and speed. It sends a screenshot-based issue list to the developer so fixes are clear.
before: Check GA4 and Google Ads pixels.
Run a speed test and write notes.
after: Agent opens each page and runs the checklist.
Agent tests forms and tracking tags.
Agent captures mobile screenshots.
Agent writes an issue list with page links.
Human: fixes issues and approves launch.

opportunities.title: Competitor post digest for content planning
opportunities.description: An agent collects public posts from chosen competitor accounts and groups them by theme, format, and hook. It sends a weekly digest to help your team plan, without copying claims or creative.
after: Agent collects public posts from a set list.
Agent groups posts by theme, format, and hook.
Agent sends a weekly digest to Slack.
Human: reviews the digest and picks ideas.
Agent saves the digest to the campaign folder.

roadmap.title: Low-effort agents with human review
items: Build an approved FAQ bank for common comments and DMs.
Connect Slack, Google Workspace, and Meta Business Suite to the first agents.
Start the comments and DMs agent with human approval for all public replies.
Start the copy drafting agent for social captions and ad variants.
Start the monthly report data pull agent for one or two friendly clients.

roadmap.title: Client workflows and finance
items: Add the client approval tracker and reminder agent.
Add weekly call recaps with human review before sending.
Add invoice reminders and subscription renewal flags.
Add landing page launch checks for the developer.
Train account managers and social managers on review steps and escalation rules.

roadmap.title: Creative and planning support
items: Add ad resize prep and export naming for the design team.
Add the competitor post digest for content planning.
Expand agents to more client accounts after privacy checks.
Review hours saved, error rates, and client feedback every month.
Refine FAQ banks, tone guides, and report templates from agent logs.

risks.risk: Client data privacy and platform rules are not followed.
risks.mitigation: Only connect approved client accounts, get written consent, limit agent access to what is needed, and review DMs before replies go out.

risks.risk: An AI reply or client email damages a brand or relationship.
risks.mitigation: Keep human approval for all public replies and client emails. Use an approved FAQ bank and escalate sensitive topics to an account manager.

risks.risk: Integrations break or become hard to maintain.
risks.mitigation: Start with Google Workspace, Slack, and Meta. Add one tool at a time. Document each connection and assign one owner per agent.

risks.risk: The team does not adopt the agents or sees them as extra work.
risks.mitigation: Assign an owner per agent, hold a 30-minute weekly review, and show hours saved per role. Start with the tasks people dislike most.

risks.risk: Report numbers are wrong before they reach a client.
risks.mitigation: Have the agent pull raw data, then require a human check against platform dashboards before any client report is sent.
